text:
lina: Quick summary from the quant bakeoff run this morning — FP8/GPTQ/AWQ/INT8 across Llama2-13B and Llama2-70B variants. Results attached inline. Overall: FP8 gives best perf for 13B with ~2.6x speedup and ~7% memory drop; GPTQ (8-bit per-block) is most consistent for 70B with <1.8% accuracy delta on our QA evals; AWQ shows very low mem but sometimes spikes in instruction-following tests. INT8 (symmetric) is fast but ~3-6% quality regression on code generation tasks. Pls read notes below and flag anything urgent.
samir: Nice. Which exact metrics are we using for "quality" here?
lina: primary: exact-match and F1 on SQuAD-like QA set; secondary: average BLEU/ROUGE for summarization, pass@1 for code tasks, and a custom safety/toxicity gate. Also track perplexity on our internal prompt-holdout.
maria: Did you run the latency distribution under our hosted 99th percentile SLO config? Need p50/p95/p99 numbers before we set canary weights.
lina: yes. Quick numbers (Llama2-13B): fp32 baseline p50=220ms p95=480ms p99=860ms; awq p50=95ms p95=220ms p99=510ms. GPTQ p50=120ms p95=260ms p99=560ms. int8 p50=90ms p95=210ms p99=600ms. Accuracy deltas vs fp32 on QA: awq -2.4%, gptq -0.9%, fp8 -0.6%, int8 -3.8%.
zack: For Dedicated and Private deployments, do we expect the same deltas? Or are they hardware dependent?
lina: hardware matters. On A100 vs H100 we saw slightly better preservation of accuracy on H100 for fp8 and GPTQ (H100 quant kernels behave nicer). For older GPUs (V100) AWQ had more variance. So rollout profiles must be hardware-aware.
samir: Good call. Proposal for an automated canary policy:
maria: +1 show the YAML so oncall can wire it into console rollout.
lina: here's a minimal rollout config we've been testing (paste):

```
rollout:
  model_variant: llm-13b-awq
  canary:
    duration: 30m
    steps:
      - traffic: 1%
        metrics:
          latency_p95: <= 1.2 * baseline
          qa_f1_drop: <= 3.0
      - traffic: 10%
        metrics:
          latency_p95: <= 1.3 * baseline
          qa_f1_drop: <= 2.0
      - traffic: 50%
        metrics:
          latency_p95: <= 1.5 * baseline
          qa_f1_drop: <= 1.5
  fallback:
    - target: llm-13b-gptq
      trigger: qa_f1_drop > 2.5 or latency_p95 > 2.0 * baseline
    - target: llm-13b-fp32
      trigger: persistent_error_rate > 0.01
  scope:
    hosts: [hosted, dedicated]
    hw_tags: [h100, a100]
```

samir: Where does private (VPC/on-prem) fit here? We should default to more conservative thresholds and lower initial traffic.
lina: agreed — for private we do: start 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% and stricter qa_f1_drop thresholds (1.0 max). Also require a manual approval if hardware tag includes anything older than a100.
zack: How about fallback granularity? Can we fallback per-customer-route instead of global? Some customers care more about latency than quality.
maria: Console supports per-route policies now (we tested in staging). We can set a policy map per customer tier: enterprise -> quality-first (fallback to gptq/fp32 quickly), startup -> latency-first (fallback to int8 or awq). We must ensure cost alerts also fire.
lina: Implementation notes: bakeoff artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-quant-bakeoffs/1713302400/ with detailed eval logs. We also stored per-prompt diffs to help triage hallucination/regression clusters. Short script to reproduce a variant locally:

```
docker run --gpus all redwood/quant-bake:latest \
  --model llm-13b --quant awq --batch 1 --eval-set qa_holdout.json --out results.json
```

deploy-bot: automated-canary-checker posted: canary run for llm-13b-awq step 1 (1% traffic) completed. p95=210ms (1.1x baseline), qa_f1_drop=1.8% — PASS :white_check_mark:
samir: Great. Any known failure modes? You mentioned instruction-following spikes earlier.
lina: yes — AWQ sometimes underperforms on long context instruction-following where KV cache patterns are heavy; we flagged a tokenizer alignment bug that affects probability calibration on a small prompt subset. Root cause looks like quant-induced logits scaling in a particular attention block; working with model-conversion to patch scaling constants.
zack: Timeline to promote gptq or awq to hosted default for 13B?
lina: if next 48h canary steps remain green on hosted/a100 and we get one dedicated cluster run, I'd be comfortable promoting gptq as default for non-enterprise tier. AWQ remains experimental until we fix the instr-following cluster.
maria: I'll add the canary policy to the rollout dashboard and set alert channels to #eng-oncall and #eng-ml. Also adding automatic rollback to exclude private deployments unless approved.
samir: One more ask — include a small evaluation that measures toxicity/regression on our policy evasion set. Quant changes sometimes increase unsafe answer propensity.
lina: done, included in the S3 folder: toxicity_scan.csv and prompt-diffs. Preliminary shows no significant uplift for gptq/awq, small increase for int8 on a handful of adversarial prompts.
zack: thanks team. Action items: lina follow up on tokenizer scaling patch, maria create rollout in console with hardware scoping, samir update infra to tag hosts by kernel-quant-capability. I'll sync with growth on messaging. :thumbsup:
lina: thanks — i'll post a short thread with the key numbers for the ops playbook and link to the s3 artifacts.
